newsitem.title: CYPRUS: FOCUS-Cyprus court rejects Slovenian cash claim.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cyprus court rejects Slovenian cash claim.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Tuesday lifted an injunction freezing deposits from former Yugoslavia's national bank at a Cyprus-based institution.

The injunction was imposed by a district court in capital Nicosia 13 months ago after Slovenia laid claim to millions of dollars allegedly stashed in the Cyprus unit of Beogradska banka by the former national bank after the break-up of the country.

"Slovenia alleged that the accounts of the National Bank of Yugoslavia with Beogradska Banka Cyprus contained funds belonging to Slovenian banks and citizens but failed to support this with evidence," Beogradska Banka said in a statement issued in Nicosia.

In its ruling, the district court lifted a year-old injunction which froze the accounts of the former national bank in Beogradska Banka in Nicosia, which operates as an offshore banking unit on the island.
The initial court injunction was issued in the absence of Beogradska Banka, which later contested the order in court.
The government of Slovenia claim was for 900 million marks ($480 million), which Slovenia said was deposited in the national bank before the break-up of former Yugoslavia.

"After a long trial that lasted almost one year, the court issued today its decision and cancelled in full the interlocutory order and dismissed the application of Slovenia with costs being adjudged against Slovenia," the Beogradska Banka statement said.

The court ruling, according to Beogradska Banka, stated that Slovenia failed to comply with its legal duty when applying to the court in the absence of defendants to make a full and frank disclosure of the relevant facts and the nature of their claim.
The ruling also stated that a Cypriot court could not entertain disputes between a foreign govermment and a federal institution in a third country because of state immunity.
Cypriot lawyer Nicos Georgiades, one of a team of lawyers who represented Slovenia during the case, said an appeal was being considered.

"We believe that the Cyprus courts have the juristiction to adjucicate on the merits of this case since the actual money which the Slovenian government claims against the national bank of former Yugoslavia is deposited within the Cyprus juristiction." he told Reuters.
